handback.title: A rejected model key is reported as a rejected key
handback.summary: When the provider refuses the agent's key, the owner is told to replace the key, not shown a planner bug.
handback.user_story: When a model key stops working, the owner learns which secret to replace, at setup and on every failed run.

acceptance_criteria.text: When the agent's output shows a login or key failure, the run ends as Model key rejected, not missing hand-back.
acceptance_criteria.words: After the agent step, if its output shows a login or key failure (401/403, invalid or expired token, failed to authenticate), end the run as "Model key rejected" instead of checking for the hand-back file.

edge_cases.case: The provider says the token expired.
The agent ran fine but left no plan: the missing plan is still reported.

acceptance_criteria.text: When a run ends as Model key rejected, its comment names the repo secret the settings use for that agent.
acceptance_criteria.words: The issue comment names the secret the settings use for that agent (e.g. `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`)

edge_cases.case: The settings name another secret for the planner.

acceptance_criteria.text: When a run ends as Model key rejected, its comment says the provider refused the key: replace the secret.
acceptance_criteria.words: says the provider refused it: make a new one and replace the repo secret.
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: It is one fixed message; the failure cases belong to the first criterion.

acceptance_criteria.text: When a run ends as Model key rejected, no part of the key appears on its comment or record.
acceptance_criteria.words: Never print any part of the key.

edge_cases.case: No secret was given to the record step to remove.

acceptance_criteria.text: When the agent key is present, the setup audit makes one tiny call with it; when absent, none.
acceptance_criteria.words: The setup audit checks the agent key once with a tiny call (when the key is present)

edge_cases.case: No key is given to the audit: no call is made.
The provider accepts the key: nothing is reported.

acceptance_criteria.text: When the provider rejects the key at setup, the audit reports it as one line naming its secret.
acceptance_criteria.words: reports a rejected key as one line, so an owner learns at install time, not on their first issue.
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: The accepted and absent key cases are covered under the criterion before.

raises.label: Workflow change
raises.text: The audit key check needs the audit workflows to pass the key. May the worker change them? Plan assumes yes.
raises.evidence: `.github/workflows/audit.yml` gets only `DOKIMA_APP_KEY`; `entry.yml` audit job passes only that.
